verdict: Sales rose 8% to $6.86B on price increases and the Suvinil deal, but higher raw-material costs squeezed margins, so net income slipped 1% to $821M.

segments.name: Paint Stores Group
segments.note: Sherwin-Williams' own stores selling to professional painters and contractors — same-store sales rose 3.9%.

segments.name: Consumer Brands Group
segments.note: DIY brands like Valspar and HGTV Home sold through retailers, boosted by the Suvinil acquisition in Brazil.

segments.name: Performance Coatings Group
segments.note: Industrial coatings for cars, packaging, buildings and other manufactured products.

segments.name: Administrative & other
segments.note: Tiny corporate and other sales that do not sit in the three main groups.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the paint stores, sales reps and head office.

flow.otherDetail: Other income of -$139M is interest expense of $139M plus $6M of other expense, minus $6M of interest income (rounded components).

takeaways.title: All three businesses grew sales
takeaways.text: Paint Stores rose 5%, Consumer Brands 22% (helped by buying Suvinil in Brazil) and Performance Coatings 9%, taking total sales to $6.86B.

takeaways.title: Margins were squeezed by costs
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell from 49.2% to 47.8% as raw material and supply chain costs rose, so net income slipped 1% to $821M despite higher sales.

takeaways.title: Cash went back to shareholders
takeaways.text: Sherwin-Williams returned $749M to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and share buybacks.

oneTimers: Adjusted EPS of $3.63 excludes Valspar acquisition-related amortization and severance and restructuring costs; GAAP EPS was $3.38. Full-year guidance includes $0.82 per share of Valspar amortization and $0.11 of severance and restructuring.
footerNote: Sherwin-Williams reports in millions to one decimal place; figures are rounded to whole $M (tax of $242.5M rounds to $243M), so the statement balances exactly.
